parts.text: A student takes three independent mini-tests in Physics, Chemistry, and Biology. The probabilities that the student achieves a grade A in these tests are $0.75$, $0.60$, and $0.80$ respectively. Find the probability that the student achieves a grade A in all three tests.

A golfer attempts to qualify for a tournament. The probability that the golfer qualifies on the first round is $0.40$. If the golfer fails to qualify on the first round, they are permitted a second round, where the probability of qualifying is $0.55$. Find the probability that the golfer qualifies for the tournament within the two rounds.

questions.title: Total Probability with Unknown Defect Rate

parts.text: A factory produces light bulbs on two production lines, Line 1 and Line 2. A light bulb is selected at random. The probability that it came from Line 1 is $0.4$, and the probability that it came from Line 2 is $0.6$. The probability that a bulb produced by Line 1 is defective is $p$, and the probability that a bulb produced by Line 2 is defective is $3p$. Given that the overall probability of a randomly selected bulb being defective is $0.11$, find the value of $p$.
Two fair four-sided dice, each with faces numbered 1, 2, 3, and 4, are rolled simultaneously. Find the probability that the sum of the two numbers obtained is at least 6.

A four-colour spinner has sectors coloured Red, Blue, and Green. In any single spin, the probabilities of landing on Red, Blue, and Green are $0.5$, $0.3$, and $0.2$ respectively. The spinner is spun 4 times independently. Find the probability of obtaining Red exactly twice, Blue exactly once, and Green exactly once.

Bag A contains 4 white counters and 2 black counters. Bag B contains 3 white counters and 5 black counters. One counter is chosen at random from Bag A and transferred to Bag B. A counter is then chosen at random from Bag B. Find the probability that both the transferred counter and the counter chosen from Bag B are white.

In a coastal town, the weather on each day is classified as either Sunny ($S$) or Rainy ($R$). On Monday, the probability of rain is $0.4$. On any subsequent day, the probability of rain is $0.7$ if it rained on the preceding day, and $0.2$ if it was sunny on the preceding day. Find the probability that it is sunny on both Monday and Tuesday.
Find the probability that the first rainy day of the week is Wednesday.

An archer shoots arrows at a target until hitting the bullseye or until 3 shots have been taken. The probability of hitting the bullseye on the first shot is $0.3$. For any subsequent shot, the probability of hitting the bullseye is $0.5$ if the immediately preceding shot was a miss. Find the probability that the archer hits the bullseye on the second shot.
Find the probability that the archer hits the bullseye within the 3 shots.

At a busy roundabout, vehicles independently take one of three exits: Exit A with probability $0.4$, Exit B with probability $0.4$, and Exit C with probability $0.2$. Three vehicles enter the roundabout one after another. Find the probability that all three vehicles take different exits.
Find the probability that exactly two of the three vehicles take the same exit.

questions.title: Urn Transfer with Variable Red Discs

parts.text: Urn 1 contains 5 red discs and 3 blue discs. Urn 2 contains $n$ red discs and 4 blue discs, where $n$ is a positive integer. A disc is chosen at random from Urn 1 and transferred into Urn 2. A disc is then chosen at random from Urn 2. Find an expression in terms of $n$, simplified as a single algebraic fraction, for the probability that both chosen discs are red.
Given that the overall probability that the disc chosen from Urn 2 is red is equal to $\frac{9}{16}$, find the value of $n$.
Three fair standard six-sided dice are thrown simultaneously. Find the probability that the sum of the scores on the three dice is equal to 6.
Given that the sum of the scores on the three dice is equal to 6, find the probability that at least two of the dice show the same score.

Over a 4-day outdoor festival (Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday), the weather on each day is classified as either Wet ($W$) or Dry ($D$). On Thursday (Day 1), the probability of a Wet day is $0.2$. On each subsequent day:
- If the preceding day was Wet, the probability that the day is Wet is $0.6$.
- If the preceding day was Dry, the probability that the day is Wet is $0.3$.

Find the probability that all 4 days of the festival are Dry.
Find the probability that Saturday (Day 3) is Wet.
Find the probability that there is exactly one Wet day during the 4-day festival.

In a school quiz league, teams score points in independent rounds. In any single round, Team Alpha scores 3 points with probability $0.5$, 1 point with probability $0.3$, and 0 points with probability $0.2$. In a session of 4 independent rounds, find the probability that Team Alpha scores a total of exactly 7 points.
In a separate competition, Team Alpha plays 3 independent rounds. Let $T$ be the total points scored across the 3 rounds. Find the probability that $T \ge 6$.
Given that Team Alpha scores a total of at least 6 points across the 3 rounds, find the probability that they scored 3 points in every round.
